plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the cross-ratio, a projective invariant used in single-view 3D scene understanding. It shows sets of collinear points P, Q, and R related by the cross-ratio, projected from a center of projection O. The point R1 lies at infinity because the line connecting the R points is parallel to the line passing through O, P1, and Q1. The figure demonstrates how if two sets of points, related by a projection, have the same ordering, then their cross ratio will be preserved.

interactionPlan.concept: The cross-ratio of four collinear points is preserved under projection from any center, so three point-sets that are projections of one another (P, Q, R) share one invariant value even when one point lies at infinity.
elements: center of projection O (black dot) at far left with label 'O'
four black rays (a pencil of lines) emanating from O toward the right
magenta transversal line carrying P1, P2, P3, P4 (one point per ray), with point dots and labels P1..P4
magenta transversal line (steeper) carrying Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 with point dots and labels Q1..Q4
magenta transversal line (shallow, upper-right) carrying R2, R3, R4 with point dots and labels R2..R4
annotation 'R1 -> infinity' with a rightward arrow on the shallow transversal, indicating R1 is the point at infinity because that line is parallel to the bottom ray through O, P1, Q1
live cross-ratio readout showing CR(P), CR(Q), CR(R) as three equal numeric values
draggable handles on each P, Q, R point and on O

interactions.teaches: Sliding any P, Q, or R point along its transversal changes all three cross-ratio values together but they remain exactly equal to one another, demonstrating that the cross-ratio is invariant under projection between the collinear sets

Moving the center of projection O re-fans the rays and re-projects every point, yet the three cross-ratios stay equal, showing the invariance holds for any choice of projection center, not just the drawn one

interactions.label: Highlight collinear set
interactions.teaches: Stepping through P, Q, R one at a time isolates each transversal and shows its four points carry the same cross-ratio as the others, making the shared invariant explicit set by set

demo_steps.title: One invariant, three lines
demo_steps.narration: P, Q and R are three collinear four-point sets that are projections of one another through O; the readout shows CR(P) = CR(Q) = CR(R), the projective invariant.

demo_steps.title: Inspect each set
demo_steps.narration: Highlight the P set, then Q, then R: each transversal's four points yield the identical cross-ratio, confirming the value travels unchanged across the projection.

demo_steps.title: Drag the points
demo_steps.narration: Drag P, Q or R points along their lines: every cross-ratio value updates live, but the three stay locked equal — the invariant survives any motion of the points on their lines.

demo_steps.title: Drag the center, note R1 at infinity
demo_steps.narration: Drag O to a new location and the whole projection re-fans while the cross-ratios remain equal; notice R1 sits at infinity because its transversal is parallel to the bottom ray, yet the invariant still holds (reducing to a simple ratio).

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Because the cross-ratio of four collinear points is unchanged by projection from any center, a value measured on an image line equals the value on the original 3D line — a projective invariant that survives even a point at infinity.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Place O as a black dot at the far left with four black rays fanning out to the right at increasing slopes (bottom ray shallow-down, top ray steep-up). Draw three magenta transversals crossing the rays: a near-vertical one holding P1(bottom)..P4(top), a steeper diagonal holding Q1..Q4, and a shallow upper-right one holding R2..R4 with an arrowed 'R1 -> infinity' label at its right end (this line is parallel to the bottom ray, hence R1 at infinity). Mark every P/Q/R as a filled black dot with serif italic subscript labels. Add a small live readout panel (top area) listing CR(P), CR(Q), CR(R) as numbers that recompute on drag and visibly stay equal. Make O and all P/Q/R points draggable handles; on drag, recompute each point as the intersection of its ray with its transversal and refresh the readout. Highlight mode tints the selected transversal and its four points while dimming the others.
